meta.jhaNotes:
- Office mishaps generally occur less frequently when compared to the number of mishaps experienced in the industrial environment. However, office workers (An employee who works in an office, especially one engaged in clerical or administrative work.) do experience mishaps and the resulting injuries can be just as painful and just as severe as their industrial counterparts. Stay focused, do not be in a rush or hurry, use the correct equipment, and report any unsafe conditions or processes. Correcting unsafe habits of seasoned employees will help teach new employees proper procedures and processes, this could be a result of complacency. Below are some potential hazards and how you can prevent them. An office environment is usually a low hazard environment, however, there can be hazards e.g. spills, left open drawers, extension cords, clutter, etc. that may increase the risk of a mishap occurring. Please keep your work area/office hazard free.
- Proper Lifting Techniques - Keep a wide base of support. Squat down, bending at the hips and knees only. Keep good posture. Slowly lift by straightening your hips and knees (not your back). Hold the load as close to your body as possible, at the level of your belly button.
- Ergonomics - Change work methods to allow an opportunity to maintain a neutral posture. Use an adjustable workstation to help maintain a neutral posture and change body positions periodically throughout the day. 
- Vehicle Operations - Seatbelt usage is mandatory. Follow all road signage to include posted speed limits. 
- Crushing Hazards - While we don’t have any severe crushing hazards in our workplace, you still need to be cognizant of closing drawers or doors and the potential of hands being caught.
- Weather - Severe weather hazards, such as tornadoes, lightning, hail, flash flooding, and downbursts, can be dangerous. Each requires a basic understanding of what to do so that you can protect yourself. The scale of weather conditions can seem daunting, ranging from high heat with humidity to torrential downpours with possible flooding. However, be prepared by knowing the weather forecast. Prepare for the types of weather hazards that are associated with wherever you are, such as tornadoes, lightning, torrential rains, and high winds. In the event of severe weather, stay away from windows and evacuate to the basement when told to do so.
- Paper Shredders – If using a shredder, keep any loose items e.g. tie, hair etc. away from the blades. Also, when emptying the shredder, unplug the power cord first.
- Fire Hazards –Bldg. 2484 has fire extinguishers. Attempt to fight the fire if possible. Fire Alarm should be activated immediately. Reference Attachment 1 for evacuation maps.
meta.emergencyNumbers: For emergencies dial 911 – inform the operator that you are on Lackland AFB, Randolph AFB, Chapman Annex, Camp Bullis, or Fort Sam Houston.
meta.medicalFacility:
1. During normal duty hours on weekdays, personnel are to report to the UCC at WHASC, or the ER at BAMC.

meta.evacuationRoute: In case of a building evacuation, the primary assembly point is the Southeast Corner of the Bleachers at the parade field and the alternate assembly point is the Gateway Club. Gather at these at the appropriate location for accountability and further guidance. Fire alarm pull stations are at each floor exit.
meta.trafficSafetyNotes:
Seat belts
Seat belts are required to be worn on base in military and civilian vehicles so equipped as directed by DAFI 91-207. In addition, child restraint systems or booster seats shall be used as prescribed by the manufacturer. Texas state law requires mandatory use of seat belts by all passengers in any vehicle so equipped off base.
Motorcycles
Motorcyclists on base must have attended a Motorcycle Safety Foundation Course and are required to wear a helmet and PPE as directed by DAFI 91-207. All riders must establish an Air Force Safety Automated System (AFSAS) account and upload all required briefings and training. Contact your unit’s Motorcycle Safety Representative for additional information.
Cell Phones
Vehicle operators on an AF installation and operators of government owned, leased, or rented vehicles, on/off an AF installation, shall not use cell phones while the vehicle is in operation, except when using a hands-free device or hands-free operating mode as directed by DAFI 91-207.
Base speed limits
Parking Lots – 10 MPH
Roadways – 30 MPH
Potential Hazards Associated with the Surrounding Local Area
Excessive speeding and driving while impaired
Construction
Stop and go traffic and road construction
Flash flooding
Dense fog
Highway speed limit is typically 65 mph; however, it varies from 55 to 70
